round1.thesis: The panel has a real idea on paper and half of one on screen. REDESIGN.md:43 states it in one sentence ("monochrome restraint + one intelligent accent; warmth through type and voice, not decoration") and §4 gives it a shape ("a conversation with a capable studio partner, plus direct access to its capabilities, plus the means to trust it" - CONVERSE dominant). The restraint half survived the trip into Qt: measured, the chat face is 0.82-0.84% chromatic in all three profiles, the wordmark is a designed lockup that never elides, the mark is the one warm note. The dominance half did not: at the 340x760 docking width the conversation gets 37/44/48% of the pane and 169-201px of chrome speaks before it does. And the "one point of view" half is fractured exactly where the idea would be visible - the accent means "intelligence/connectivity" in the brief but 79% of the panel's colour is a SEND button while connectivity is a grey ring; two selector vocabularies sit 47px apart where the before-shot had one; the type-set verb rail, the purest expression of "type not chrome", is cut mid-word in three of three profiles; and five controls are constructed as one component and repainted as another so the token table and the paint disagree. Bierut would say the idea is sound and the style has started substituting for it at the seams - the fix is not a new idea, it is holding every element to the one already written.

findings.title: The 'dominant' conversation is a plurality, not a majority, at the docking width
findings.evidence: docs/design/SYNAPSE_PANEL_REDESIGN.md §4 names CONVERSE '(dominant)'. Measured at 340x760 (harness/design_review/2026-09-05/regions_{curious,expert,ml}.json, chat.h): 282 / 338 / 366 px = 37% / 44% / 48% of the pane. Chrome before the first word (rail+ribbon+tab_row): 193 / 177 / 169 px. Act band + composer: 245 / 213 / 197 px. In curious the composer band (245) is nearly the conversation's size (282). Screens: shot_curious.png, shot_expert.png, shot_ml.png.
findings.principle: The idea is the thing; every element earns its place. If the brief says one zone dominates, the pixels must agree at the width the brief was written for.
findings.recommendation: Hold the chrome above the conversation to one band. The ribbon (46px carrying 'no scene context', synapse_panel.py:996-1005) and the profile row (47px, :1084-1104) are the two candidates; which one folds into the overflow is the Design Director's call, not mine. Target: conversation >= 50% at 340x760 in every profile, measured by the same probe.

findings.title: The accent's stated meaning and its shipped use are different things
findings.evidence: REDESIGN.md §3: 'a single accent SIGNAL for intelligence/connectivity'. Pixel count on shot_expert.png (Pillow, chroma > 24): 2181 chromatic px of 258,400 (0.84%); SEND fill (SIGNAL_DEEP #627A93, tokens.py:239, qss.py:241-248) = 1714 px (79%); the active-tab underline (qss.py:128-130) is most of the rest. findings.principle: One point of view. An accent that means one thing in the brief and another on screen is decoration wearing a meaning it does not carry.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile in one direction: either re-state the accent's role in tokens.py (accent = the artist's next action) so the doc matches the panel, or move the accent to the connectivity state and let SEND be a quiet verb (Enter already sends - khint :1952). Human decides which; do not leave the two documents disagreeing.

findings.title: The idle panel says 'nothing yet' eight different ways
findings.evidence: Distinct idle strings: 'Standing by' (synapse_panel.py:714; face_work.py:196), 'Not connected' (:769), 'no scene context' (:1002), 'Ready. What are we building?' findings.principle: Restraint - a thousand no's for every yes. One idea says the quiet state once.
findings.recommendation: One idle line per face. The chat face already has the right one ('Ready. What are we building?' - it is voice, not status). The Work face's five collapse to its status line; the empty sub-sections render as absence, not as labels announcing absence.

findings.title: Praise: the restraint half of the idea is real and measurable

Wordmark: Space Grotesk, pixelSize 14, weight 700, letterSpacing 116% (WORDMARK 0.16em, tokens.py:396), x=54, bundled fonts ok, build_mismatch false (regions_expert.json); it never elides by construction (synapse_panel.py:706-712). The mark is the one warm note at ~18 px. StatusDot and MarkDot are monolinear at STROKE_PX 1.5 (tokens.py:545). Verbs are type (qss.py:161-165). The rail meter was retired as 'a fourth signal for one state' (:812-817).
findings.principle: The identity is the last thing that gives way. Here it did not give way: the lockup, the monochrome field, and the one accent held through a density system and three profiles.
findings.recommendation: Protect this as the floor. Every finding above is the other half of the same idea - dominance, meaning, one vocabulary - and none of them requires touching what already works.

round1.thesis: Typography is the voice, and this panel is speaking in two. The written system (tokens.py:357-363, REDESIGN.md:46) says the voice is a sans -- Space Grotesk for anything read as words, Space Mono only where glyphs are data -- with hierarchy from position and space, one accent, no bolding. The screen says otherwise: of 95 rendered text widgets at the docked 340px (type_census_expert_340.json, hython 22.0.400 offscreen), 61 are Space Mono, 26 Space Grotesk, 8 the host face; 40 are uppercase; ten different tracking settings are live through four mechanisms the token doc says do not exist. The scale on paper (19/15/12/11/10) is not the scale on screen (15/14/12/11/10, plus a 21 on the review verdict): the 19px display role has no consumer and the two largest sizes that ship are literals. The single worst consequence is that the tracked-caps verb rail -- the panel's spoken actions -- cannot fit its own words at 340 in any profile, and 21px of letterspace is the entire overflow (LABEL 0.15em = 301px vs a 280px well; 0em = 272; sentence-case sans 12px = 248). Bierut would not add anything here; he would cut: one family for words, one for data, three tracking values, three honest weights (the bundle has no SemiBold face, so 600 renders as 500 or 700 depending on code path), one floor, and a type audit that counts widgets instead of constants. The wordmark is the exception and the proof: 69px hint held at 340 and at 280 in every density, Space Grotesk 700 14px 116% -- the identity is the one element that never gives way, which is exactly the standard the rest of the type should be held to.

findings.title: Verb rail cannot say its own words at 340 in 3/3 profiles; the tracking is the overflow
findings.evidence: Rendered widths vs sizeHints (type_census_*_340.json, DsVerb rows): expert OPTIMIZE 59/65, BUILD HDA 58/73; curious EXPLAIN 48/57, OPTIMIZE 47/65, BUILD HDA 48/73; ml BUILD HDA 68/73. Screenshots design/rhythm_pd/after_r3/{expert,curious,ml}/panel_direct_chat.png show ')PTIMIZE' 'UILD HD.' / 'XPLAIN' 'PTIMIZ' 'ILD HI'. Exact demand at 11px Space Mono (verb_tracking.json, hint=advance+1, gaps 4x16 measured from x=30/103/144/219/293): LABEL 0.15em (synapse_panel.py:1892-1893) = 301px vs 280px content (340 - 2*GUTTER 30); LABEL_SM 296; SEND 0.08 = 288; DATA 0.03 = 278 fits; 0em = 272 fits; sans title-case 12px = 248 fits by 32. At the 280 contract (type_census_expert_280.json) every verb is 38px wide against 57-73 hints.
findings.principle: The idea is the thing and style serves it; typography is the voice. A voice that clips its own verbs is not a voice, and here the styling (tracked mono caps, qss.py:160 'verbs read as type') is the sole cause of the clip.
findings.recommendation: Drop the verbs to the doctrine's own rule for prose-shaped chrome: sans, sentence case, no tracking (248px, fits at 340 with 32px spare, and at the 280 contract with the Aa duplicate removed). If mono caps are kept as a taste decision, tracking must fall to DATA 0.03 or 0 (278/272) and the human should know that leaves 2-8px of margin. Do not add a breakpoint or icon collapse to rescue a type choice.

findings.title: Two-thirds of the voice is typewriter, against the system's own doctrine
findings.evidence: type_census_expert_340.json family_hist (95 visible text widgets, w>0): Space Mono 61 (64%), Space Grotesk 26 (27%), host face 8 (8%); same split in curious and ml. tokens.py:357-363: 'Mono is for CODE, sans is for everything else ... setting them in a typewriter face made the panel read like a terminal emulator rather than a tool'; REDESIGN.md:46 same. Mono today: verbs EXPLAIN/FIX/OPTIMIZE/BUILD HDA (synapse_panel.py:1892), ribbon Connect/Corpus, CHAT/TOKEN and profile pills (:1065-1100), author/meter/khint (:724-744, :1953), and every work-face caption ('waiting for work', 'no steps yet', 'Awaiting telemetry...' in after_r3/expert/face_work.png).
findings.principle: One point of view. The document holds a sans-led view of the product; the screen holds a mono-led one. Two views is none.
findings.recommendation: Pick the doctrine (it is the right one for a panel docked inside Houdini's sans UI): Space Grotesk for anything read as words -- actions, captions, status, pills; Space Mono only for ids, paths, counts, code and the section eyebrow. That single move also resolves T2 and most of T4.

findings.title: The type scale on paper is not the scale on screen
findings.evidence: TYPE_ROLES ladder 19/15/12/11 (+SIZE_MICRO 10) at tokens.py:311-316, 365-373. Rendered px across four faces at 340 (type_census_expert_340.json px_hist): 12 x43, 11 x41, 10 x6, 14 x4, 15 x1; no 19px widget anywhere (rg role="display" in panel/: zero consumers). 14 is a literal (synapse_panel.py:704 tracked_font('WORDMARK', 14)), 21 is a literal (face_review.py:227 tracked_font('DISPLAY', 21, weight=500)), 15px title ships on one label (synapse_panel.py:1797). audit_panel.py:99-108 prints 'hierarchy: 5 distinct steps [ok]' from the constants, not from widgets (audit_strict_TYPE.txt).
findings.principle: A system must survive its designer and every state. A ladder nobody climbs is a list of numbers; the ladder the artist sees is 10/11/12/14/15(+21).
findings.recommendation: Make the token ladder the shipped ladder: promote 14 (mark) and 21 (verdict) into TYPE_ROLES or retire them, delete SIZE_HERO/display (zero consumers; test_type_scale_native still holds >=4 steps with 10/11/12/15), and have the audit count rendered pixel sizes rather than constants (escalate: I do not edit audit_panel.py).

findings.title: Ten tracking settings, four mechanisms; the token doc denies three of them
findings.evidence: type_census_expert_340.json spacing_hist: 100% x29, 115% x34, 106% x12, 108% x5, 116% x4, 103% x4, 122% x1, 112% x1, abs 0.5px x4, abs 1.0px x1. Mechanisms: QFont PercentageSpacing (fontload.py:181), QFont AbsoluteSpacing (components.py:47 via TYPE_ROLES 4th column), QSS letter-spacing (qss.py:533,537,560,584,587), HTML letter-spacing (message_formatter.py:302, 1.2px). tokens.py:383-385: 'Tracking lives on QFont ... NEVER in QSS (Qt QSS has no letter-spacing)' -- probe on Qt 6.8.3: QLabel sizeHint 56 -> 96px with 'letter-spacing: 5px', font().letterSpacing()=5.0; QTextDocument idealWidth 64 -> 104, fragment fontLetterSpacing 5.0 (type_census_report.txt PROBES). TRACKING_EM has 9 entries; BRAND 0.286 and BODY have zero consumers (rg), and rhythm.py:65-69 borrows SEND and DATA*2 for label/tag. Adjacent steps at 11px: 103/106/108 = 0.33/0.66/0.88px per glyph.
findings.principle: Restraint: a thousand no's for every yes. Sub-pixel tracking steps are decisions nobody can see, and a mechanism the doc says cannot exist is a state the system cannot survive.
findings.recommendation: Three tracking values -- WORDMARK 0.16, EYEBROW (one value, ~0.10, shared by label and tag), DATA 0.03 -- and one owner. Delete BRAND, LABEL_SM, DISPLAY, BODY and the TYPE_ROLES absolute-px column; strip the QSS/HTML letter-spacing sites; correct the tokens.py:383-385 claim.

findings.title: SEMIBOLD is a name without a face; the same token renders 500 or 700 by code path
findings.evidence: Bundled Space Grotesk registers styles Light/Regular/Medium/Bold (type_census_*.json styles_registered) -- no SemiBold instance from SpaceGrotesk-Variable.ttf (fontload.py:28). WEIGHT_SEMIBOLD=600 (tokens.py:352). Probe: QFont weight 600 resolves to style 'Medium'; setBold -> 700 'Bold'. components.py:45 f.setBold(weight >= 600) and fontload.py:176-177 'if bold or weight >= 600: setBold' turn every 600 into 700 (wordmark weight=600 -> census weight 700; title 'Describe the HDA you want' 600 -> 700), while QSS font-weight 600 on DsButton renders the Medium face (census: Generate HDA weight 600, style Medium). qss.py writes a hidden fourth weight 700 as WEIGHT_SEMIBOLD + WEIGHT_MEDIUM - WEIGHT_REGULAR eleven times (:533,:543,:544,:560,:587,:630,:633,:642,:653,:666,:676). weight_hist 400 x71, 500 x17, 700 x5, 600 x2: hierarchy is rightly not carried by bolding.
findings.principle: Typography is the voice; a weight is a word in that voice. The system names a weight it cannot draw, then draws two different ones under that name.
findings.recommendation: Name what the bundle has: REGULAR 400, MEDIUM 500, BOLD 700. Replace WEIGHT_SEMIBOLD with BOLD where setBold already wins (wordmark, title) and with MEDIUM where QSS already resolves there; delete the arithmetic 700. Keep the discipline of near-zero bolding -- it is working.

findings.title: A third family leaks in: eight widgets carry no family at all
findings.evidence: type_census_expert_340.json family_hist host face = 8: ChatDisplay DsChatTranscript widget font (placeholder 'Ready. What are we building?'), _GrowingInput DsInput, HDA face QTextEdit DsInput, QComboBox 'SOP', QCheckBox 'Include help text', DsButton 'Generate HDA' and 'Main menu'. qss.py:21 'No font-family: inherit Houdini's app-level UI font (native)'. chat_display.py:157-162 applies Space Grotesk to the document default font but not the widget font. findings.title: Three things named label, three appliers on the wordmark, three ways to set caps

findings.principle: A system must survive its designer: three vocabularies for one word survive nobody's handover.

round1.thesis: A system survives its designer when its vocabulary is semantic enough that the next hand reaches for a role and gets the right answer without reading the token file. Read as one system, tokens.py + rhythm.py + qss.py is a good 4pt grid wearing nine role names that resolve, at runtime, to two gap sizes (24/16/12 and 6/4/3) plus zero; card and group are indistinguishable, stack and parm_row are indistinguishable, row is dead, and parm_row is a QSS column-width hook on layout-less labels rather than a rhythm at all. The system holds the three densities cleanly (the compositor's one property does scale every marked gap, measured) and the Aa ladder correctly stays out of chrome, but it leaks at every seam where two appliers meet: the same c.Pill class in one 47px strip carries 115% tracking as an underline tab and 106% as a filled square chip, because a tracked_font and a rhythm role both fire and the later one wins; the "999 pill" radius rung is a CSS idiom Qt 6.8.3 silently discards; the grid has no hairline rung so six 1px/2px literals live behind exemptions; nested QLayouts can never carry a role because the applier walks widgets; the alternate chat entry and three state widgets apply "standard" regardless of profile; bridge-down shows two contradictory status phrases from a token table that promises one vocabulary; and the docking floor is a measured number written into a YAML prose string and read back by regex, with no breakpoint token anywhere to say when a collapsed label returns. The 280 contract is a promise; 393/361/345 is the truth; 400/380/380 is the truth rounded up and called a bound. Restraint would be fewer roles that mean more, one applier per property, and a docking rule that lives in the token file where the next designer will look for it.

findings.title: Docking width is a patch: 280 promised, 393/361/345 measured, 400/380/380 written in prose
findings.evidence: tokens.py:619 PANEL_MIN_WIDTH = 280; probe_*.json panel_minimumSize = [280, ...] but panel_minimumSizeHint = [393,353] airy / [361,337] standard / [345,329] tight at 340x760. .synapse/contracts/docking-minimums.yaml carries 'RULING R3-01 ... airy is wider by design - the figure is 400, standard/tight stay 380. Interim toward the 280 contract' and tests/test_panel_rhythm_docking.py:85-86 recovers the three widths from the feature-description string with re.findall(r'<= (\d+)px wide at (airy|standard|tight)'). The only 280 test (tests/panel/test_docking.py:128-140) checks the composer cap at that width, not that content fits. No breakpoint or reappear-width token exists (grep across tokens.py, synapse_panel.py, PANEL_RHYTHM_SPEC.md, PANEL_REGION_MAP.md: 0 hits); five rail labels collapse via QSizePolicy.Ignored at synapse_panel.py:833-835 with no rule for when they return.
findings.principle: The client's problem, not the designer's ego: the artist docks at 340 in a dark Houdini UI. A bound that is the measurement rounded up, stored in a comment and parsed by regex, is a record of what happened, not a system that decides what fits.
findings.recommendation: Either make 280 true (a verb rail that collapses to glyphs below a named DOCK_COLLAPSE_PX token, and a documented reappear rule for the Ignored labels) or move the contract to the measured floor and say so in tokens.py. In both cases the per-density widths belong beside PANEL_MIN_WIDTH in the token file, not in YAML prose. Human decision; escalate with the three numbers.

findings.title: The grid has no hairline rung; nested QLayouts can never carry a role
findings.evidence: Census on master (harness/design_review/2026-09-05/rhythm_census.md, measurement_complete True): 16 residual spacing sites, 1 inline sheet, 0 raw hex, 17 exemption tags. Six residuals are off-ladder literals: face_review.py:271,299 setSpacing(1), integrity_readout.py:82 setSpacing(1), face_work.py:226 setSpacing(2), chat_panel.py:425 setSpacing(2), recall_card.py:115 setSpacing(0); the exemption text at integrity_readout.py:81-82 says 'no role expresses 1px'. Runtime (probe_expert.json off_grid_layout_spacings): four live layouts at 1-2px inside FaceReview, FaceWork, IntegrityReadout. Ten of sixteen exemptions read 'nested layout has no widget owner; wrapping changes the hierarchy' because rhythm.apply (rhythm.py:86-108) walks widget.children() and reads widget.property, so a bare QLayout is unreachable by design.
findings.principle: A system survives every state only if every state has a name; an exemption tag is the system admitting a name is missing.
findings.recommendation: Add a hairline/seam rung (0-1px) to the role table so IntegrityReadout and the recall card stop being exceptions, and either let the applier accept a role on a layout object or state in the spec that unowned layouts are outside the system. Owners: FaceReview, FaceWork, IntegrityReadout, RecallCard, SynapseChatPanel.

findings.title: Density has three inheritance paths; HDA faces and the alternate entry never see airy/tight
findings.evidence: Path A: compositor.py:243 stamps density on the root and :271 rhythm.apply(panel, density) walks the whole tree. Path B: ancestor walk in qss.py:712-720 (sweep_a_refresh_rhythm, gate cards) and :916-931 (prepare_sweep_b_popup). Path C: bare rhythm.apply(self) with no density = 'standard' at hda_views.py:33,141,243, working_indicator.py:240, recall_card.py:146 (rhythm.py:74 default). The recall card is rescued because it is built inside a region builder before :271; the HDA DescribeView/BuildingView/ResultView are owned by chat_panel.py:196-198, whose only sheet install is install_sweep_a_root (chat_panel.py:247 -> qss.py:516-520, density = root.property or 'standard') with no compositor, so design/rhythm_pd/after_r3/expert/hda_result.png is a standard-density face in every profile.
findings.principle: A system must survive every state: a state that reaches the artist through a side door still has to obey the one property that drives the rhythm.

findings.title: Praise: one property, one grid, zero raw hex, and the density lever measurably works
findings.evidence: Census: 0 raw hex sites outside designsystem/, 1 inline sheet (the root install at synapse_panel.py:348), 16 residual spacing sites all tagged. Probe: every role gap steps exactly round(base x 1.5/1.0/0.75) across the three manifests (24/16/12, 6/4/3); the Aa ladder (_cycle_font_scale) moves chat_scale 1.0 -> 1.15 and leaves chrome px (12) and group gap unchanged, exactly as tokens.py:412-418 promises; the wordmark resolves Space Grotesk 700 at 116% in all three profiles (regions_*.json) and never elides. Roles are opt-in with unmarked widgets left alone (rhythm.py:5), which is what lets the shipped panel and the legacy entry share one sheet without a rewrite.
findings.principle: The idea is the thing: a single density property driving a single grid through one sheet is the kind of system that survives its designer.
findings.recommendation: Keep the shape. Spend the next wave on fewer, truer roles and on making the contested seams (pill appliers, docking bound, bare apply) impossible rather than exempt.

round1.thesis: A thousand no's for every yes. The landed panel at 340x760 declares 34 leaf chrome elements in the direct face and renders 25 of them at non-zero size; nine are alive, laid out, paying layout gaps, and invisible (0px wide) in all three profiles. The PD wave made the rail survive the docking width by hiding, not by subtracting: the before-set screenshot shows the same nine elements clipped ("Standin", "Ctr", "Not con", "link: |"), the after-set shows them at zero width. Below the rail the pattern repeats as duplication: the same fact told two or three ways (send, /-commands, connection state, text size, engine choice), two pill rows spending 93px on five pills for one surface, and a verb rail that clips its own verbs at the width it was designed for. Bierut's argument is not that these things are ugly; it is that an element the artist cannot see, or that says what a neighbour already said, has not earned its place, and the identity (mark, wordmark, one accent on SEND, the transcript) is what should remain when they go. The file already states the doctrine (Stop state-gated, rail meter retired as "a fourth signal for one state"); this review asks that the rule be applied to the rest. Minimum viable chrome: 34 declared / 25 rendered -> 15 (+1 state-gated Stop), recovering ~102px of vertical for the transcript (338 -> ~440 at 760, +30%).

round1.thesis: Bierut's client is the VFX artist docked at 340px beside a dark network editor, asking for scene work and reading receipts; the panel must solve that person's problem, not perform the designer's. Measured live with hython 22.0.400 offscreen in all three densities, the shipped panel gets the restraint half right (0.8% chromatic pixels, one warm mark, contrast PRIMARY 8.3:1 on PANEL and a seeded worst of 5.3:1) and then fails the artist at the seat: at PANEL_PREF_WIDTH every one of the five rail state labels renders zero pixels wide, so the panel cannot say Working / Result ready / Not connected / which engine; the type-set verb rail clips its own words in 3 of 3 profiles (natural 333/301/285px against a 280px column); the undo verb lives on a face no artist-clickable control reaches; and a REVIEW-level proposal auto-surfaces a face that offers no button. Task 1 (type and send) works and is the panel's best moment, weakened only by a 52x54 attach glyph outgrowing the 60x32 SEND. The verb rail is the wrong idea at this width, not merely too wide: it mixes two prompt macros (both with / palette twins), one navigation verb and one display setting that duplicates the overflow, and collapsing it to icons (B11) would trade the typographic voice for a row that still solves nothing the palette does not. The identity holds (wordmark never elides); what gives way first is the artist's ability to read state and undo.
